company_overview_for_beginner.what_it_does: ASML, based in Veldhoven in the Netherlands, makes lithography machines: giant printers that use light to draw chip circuit patterns onto silicon wafers. It is the only company that sells EUV (extreme ultraviolet) machines, which every maker of the most advanced chips (TSMC, Samsung, Intel, memory makers) needs. It earns money two ways: selling new systems, and 'installed base management' (servicing and upgrading machines already sold).

events.summary: Q2 2026: net sales EUR 9.3bn (Reuters: EUR 9.33bn vs analysts' EUR 8.80bn), net income EUR 2.9bn (vs EUR 2.62bn expected), gross margin 54.0%, EPS EUR 7.59. ASML raised full-year 2026 sales guidance to EUR 43-45bn from EUR 36-40bn (second raise of the year) and guided Q3 to EUR 11.0-12.0bn with 55-57% gross margin. CEO Christophe Fouquet said AI investment is driving demand for advanced logic and memory chips; ASML plans about 30% more EUV and DUV capacity, and said expanded EUV capacity through 2027 is nearly fully booked.
events.why_it_matters: This is the main reason the stock is up about 75% this year: the company's own forecast rose sharply because of AI-driven chip demand.

events.summary: The US MATCH Act (introduced 2026-04-02, bipartisan) would push allies to copy US chip-tool export rules. Reported versions would stop ASML selling its older DUV immersion machines to Chinese chipmakers such as SMIC, Huawei, CXMT, YMTC and Hua Hong, and would also stop it servicing machines already installed there. In August it was reported to be on track for inclusion in the Senate defence bill (NDAA). On 2026-09-25 Dutch PM Rob Jetten was reported to be lobbying Washington and Trump against it and said he was 'very confident' of a deal. ASML expects China to be about 20% of 2026 sales (about EUR 8.8bn at the guidance midpoint, per a Dutch outlet's calculation).
events.why_it_matters: It is the largest known policy risk: it would hit both new China sales and the recurring service income from Chinese machines. It is not law yet; the final text and timing are unknown.

events.summary: Morgan Stanley reportedly cut its price target on ASML's Amsterdam shares to EUR 1,700 from EUR 1,930 and kept an Overweight (positive) rating, citing worry that near-term China demand and profit margins could disappoint after the stock's big run. Reported only by tier-3 outlets.
events.why_it_matters: It shows the main bear points ahead of Q3 results: China and margins. It is an opinion, not a fact about value.

events.summary: TSMC, ASML's largest customer, said it had no plans to adopt High-NA EUV through 2029 because the machines are 'very, very expensive' (over EUR 350m each). ASML fell 3.3% that day; Bernstein called the delay neutral or even positive, since TSMC had already signalled reluctance. In Q2, Intel began using High-NA EUV on its 18A process for some Core Ultra Series 3 chips.
events.why_it_matters: High-NA is ASML's next growth engine. How fast customers adopt it shapes revenue after 2027.

why_chain.text: About 1.96 of the 3.25 points is explained by the market (+0.58) and the chip sector (+1.38). The company-specific remainder (+1.30, z 0.81) is within a normal day's range.
Chip stocks rallied broadly that day (SOXX about +3%, Arm +8%, AMD +3%, NVIDIA +2%) on continued AI-infrastructure enthusiasm after strong recent results from AMD, NVIDIA and Broadcom.
Investors buy ASML in AI rallies because every advanced AI chip is made with its EUV machines, and the company raised 2026 guidance to EUR 43-45bn on AI-driven demand.
Positioning ahead of Q3 results on 2026-10-14 probably added to the buying, but no source names a specific ASML catalyst for Friday. Nobody published a company-specific reason.

products.name: EUV lithography systems (Low-NA NXE and High-NA EXE)
products.what_it_is: Machines that print the tiniest chip circuits using extreme ultraviolet light, which has a very short wavelength (13.5 nm).
products.analogy: A photo projector that shrinks a stencil of a circuit and 'prints' it onto a silicon wafer, like printing with an ultra-fine pen instead of a marker. High-NA is the same idea with a bigger lens that captures more light, so it draws even finer lines.
products.buyers: Makers of leading-edge logic and memory chips: TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SK hynix, Micron.
products.how_it_works: A laser hits tiny droplets of tin to create EUV light. Special mirrors reflect it through a patterned mask onto a wafer coated with light-sensitive material, repeated many times per chip layer. Customers buy the machines up front, then pay ASML for service and upgrades for years.
products.price: High-NA: over EUR 350m each (Investing.com, 2026-04-22, citing TSMC) / up to US$400m (TrendForce, 2026-05-20). Low-NA price: not available from a source checked this session.
products.sales: Q2 2026 EUV system sales EUR 3.8bn; full-year 2026 EUV net system sales growth expected over 45%; one High-NA system recognised in Q2 2026. Total new lithography systems sold in Q2 2026: 86 (all types).
products.sales_source: EUV figures: Investing.com Q2 call transcript summary, 2026-07-15 (tier 3; to verify against ASML's tier-1 release). 86 systems: ASML Q2 2026 release 6-K, 2026-07-15.
products.stage: Low-NA EUV: shipping in volume, with 2027 close to fully covered by orders. High-NA: early production use (Intel 18A); TSMC not adopting before 2029-2030; Samsung reportedly aiming for DRAM volume by 2028.
products.size_for_company: EUR 3.8bn EUV of EUR 9.3bn total Q2 net sales is about 41% (inference from the cited figures).
products.competition: No other company sells EUV machines. In older DUV machines, Nikon and Canon compete; China is developing domestic lithography (TrendForce, 2026-08-25).
products.why_investors_care: It is a monopoly product that every AI chip needs, so ASML's sales track the chipmakers' spending on AI capacity.
products.watch_next: Q3 results on 2026-10-14: EUV units and sales, comments on 2027 capacity and demand, and High-NA orders.
